title: Lifting a valuation ring through a flat scheme morphism
statement: Let $f:Y\to T$ be a flat morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism]. Let $R$ be a valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring] and let $b:\operatorname{Spec}R\to T$ be a morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Assume that the image under $b$ of the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ belongs to $f(Y)$. Then there exist a valuation ring $R\prime$, an injective local homomorphism $\iota:R\to R\prime$ (local means $\iota^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{R\prime})=\mathfrak m_R$), and a morphism $c:\operatorname{Spec}R\prime\to Y$ such that $f\circ c=b\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\iota)$. No finite-presentation, Noetherian, rank, or discreteness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Write $s$ for the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\mathfrak m_R$ for its maximal ideal. The valuation-ring condition makes $R$ a local domain: its nonunits form an ideal, since for two nonzero nonunits $a,b$ either $b=at$ or $a=bt$ for some $t\in R$, so $a+b$ is a multiple of a nonunit, and every multiple of a nonunit is a nonunit. Every element outside this proper ideal is a unit, so this is the unique maximal ideal. In particular $(0)$ is prime in $R$.

Form $Z=Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}R$, with projections $p:Z\to Y$ and $h:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. Choose $y\in Y$ with $f(y)=b(s)=t$, using the hypothesis. The ring $D=\kappa(y)\otimes_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(s)$ is nontrivial by [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-tensor-nontrivial]. By [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-maximal-ideal] it has a maximal, hence prime, ideal $P$. The point correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] applied to $(y,s,t,P)$ produces $z\in Z$ with $p(z)=y$ and $h(z)=s$. Thus the specified closed point remains in the image after base change; no rational point in the original fibre was assumed.

The morphism $h$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. Put $B=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$. By [def-weil-flat-morphism] the induced stalk map $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R,s}\to B$ is flat and local. Part (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring] identifies $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R,s}$ with $R$ by the germ isomorphism, giving a flat local homomorphism $\alpha:R\to B$. Locality gives $\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak m_R$.

Since $\alpha$ is local, the extended ideal $\mathfrak m_RB$ is contained in the proper ideal $\mathfrak n$. As $\mathfrak m_R$ is the only maximal ideal of $R$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-faithfully-flat-maximal-ideals] shows that $\alpha$ is faithfully flat. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] to the prime $(0)\subset R$ to obtain a prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ with $\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=(0)$. This is exactly the prime over zero needed for an injective extension, rather than merely a local ring map.

The quotient $A=B/\mathfrak q$ is a domain since $\mathfrak q$ is prime, and it is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak q$: every element outside this ideal has a representative outside $\mathfrak n$ and is therefore a unit, and that ideal is proper. Let $L=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. Apply [lemma-nagata-local-domain-valuation-dominates] to $A\subset L$ to obtain a valuation ring $R\prime\subset L$ containing $A$ and dominating it. (Its updated blueprint statement permits any local subring of $L$; here $L$ is even the fraction field.) Thus for $\beta:B\to A\hookrightarrow R\prime$ we have $\beta^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{R\prime})=\mathfrak n$.

Define $\iota=\beta\circ\alpha:R\to R\prime$. Its kernel is $\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=(0)$, since $A\hookrightarrow R\prime$ is injective. Moreover $\iota^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{R\prime})=\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak m_R$, so $\iota$ is local. By part (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring], the local map $\beta:\mathcal O_{Z,z}\to R\prime$ gives a morphism $d:\operatorname{Spec}R\prime\to Z$ with closed point $z$ and associated stalk map $\beta$. The two maps $h\circ d$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(\iota)$ to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ send the closed point to $s$ and induce the same local map $R\to R\prime$, namely $\beta\circ\alpha$. Injectivity of the same correspondence, with the germ identification of part (a), gives $h\circ d=\operatorname{Spec}(\iota)$. Set $c=p\circ d$. The defining identity $f\circ p=b\circ h$ of the fibre product now gives $f\circ c=b\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\iota)$, as required.
